# Overview

The premise checks showed that the delta vector δ = e_pred − e_obs is close to
90% observed-word identity, by construction. This notebook reports the
piloting framework built to look for a better representation, and the result.

The framework is a synthetic benchmark with ground truth. Controlled errors
of eight types are inserted into strong dev essays. For every error, a
**lexeme-matched clean control** (the same word form, used correctly, in
another essay) is added, together with surprising-but-unedited tokens. A fixed
evaluation battery scores any representation on it. Three families of ideas
were piloted against it in parallel (geometry of the stored vectors, the
model's hidden states, and LM-scored minimal repairs), about 45
representations in all. The finalist of each family was then scored once on a
**confirmation benchmark** built from different host essays with a different
seed, which no idea was tuned on. The success criteria were written down
before any family reported (`lab/README.md`).

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
source("src/1-predictability-benchmark/_viz_helpers.R")
LAB <- "results/study3/lab"
dev <- read_csv(file.path(LAB, "scoreboard.csv")) |> distinct(rep, .keep_all = TRUE)
conf <- read_csv(file.path(LAB, "scoreboard_conf.csv")) |> distinct(rep, .keep_all = TRUE)
family <- function(r) case_when(
  r %in% c("surprisal", "e_obs", "delta", "e_pred") ~ "baseline",
  str_starts(r, "geo") ~ "geometry", str_starts(r, "hid") ~ "hidden state",
  str_starts(r, "rep") ~ "repair", TRUE ~ "other")
```

# 1. The benchmark

| Type | Edit | Where the error becomes observable |
|---|---|---|
| DET_DEL | delete *a/an/the* | the next word |
| DET_SUB | *a/an* ↔ *the* | the determiner |
| AGR | subject–verb agreement flipped | the verb |
| VFORM | past → base, base after *to*/modal → *-ing*, participle → base | the verb |
| NUM | noun number flipped | the noun |
| PREP | preposition swapped | the preposition |
| SPELL | one-character typo, content word of 5+ letters | the word |
| HOMO | homophone or near-homophone swap (*their/there*, *its/it's*, *then/than*) | the word |
| CLEAN_SURP | unedited token above τ | — |
| MATCHED | unedited occurrence of the error's observed word form, another essay | — |

1,200 instances per type, 8,025 matched controls (SPELL has almost none,
since typos rarely occur naturally). Host essays are dev essays with Overall ≥
4.0 (confirmation: Overall = 3.5).

Building the benchmark was already informative. The share of injected errors
that clears τ is 83–90% for agreement, verb form and spelling, but 61–63% for
determiner deletion and noun number, 58% for homophones, 26% for preposition
swaps and 3% for determiner substitutions. **The 90th-percentile threshold is
largely blind to function-word substitution errors**, which limits what any
decomposition of the selected tokens can find.

# 2. The battery

The headline metric is **detect AUC**. It measures how well a cross-validated
classifier on the representation tells an error from a correct use of the
same word form. Observed-word identity scores .5 here by construction. The
others are **lexeme-disjoint F1** (error type, with test words never seen in
training), the alignment of an **unsupervised NMF** with error type vs. with
the observed word (NMI), and **word R²** (lexical leakage). Definitions are in
`lab/harness.py`.

# 3. Development scoreboard

```{r}
#| label: dev
dev |>
  mutate(family = family(rep)) |>
  select(family, rep, dim, detect_auc, lexdis_f1, type_f1, nmf_nmi_type, nmf_nmi_word, word_r2) |>
  arrange(family, desc(detect_auc)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Every representation piloted on the development bench")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dev
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
fam_col <- c(baseline = "grey40", geometry = "#E69F00", `hidden state` = "#56B4E9", repair = "#CC79A7")
p <- dev |>
  mutate(family = family(rep)) |>
  ggplot(aes(detect_auc, lexdis_f1, colour = family)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ~ filter(.x, rep %in% c("surprisal", "e_obs", "delta", "e_pred",
                                                          "geo_rel3", "hid_obs8c", "rep_repair_subpos",
                                                          "rep_mdl_plus_pos")),
                           aes(label = rep), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = fam_col, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Detect AUC (error vs. same word used correctly)",
       y = "Error-type F1 on held-out words") +
  theme_study1()
save_fig(p, "lab_scoreboard", 8, 5, dir = LAB)
p
```

Every family improves on δ once a classifier is trained on top. δ itself
detects errors worse than the four surprisal scalars (.69 vs .87). Its type
information is almost all word identity: the identity-only baseline gets the
same 9-way type F1 (.80 vs .79).

# 4. Confirmation

```{r}
#| label: conf
conf |>
  mutate(family = family(rep),
         c1 = detect_auc >= .845, c2 = lexdis_f1 > .616,
         c3 = nmf_nmi_type > nmf_nmi_word & nmf_nmi_type > .318,
         passes = c1 & c2 & c3) |>
  select(family, rep, dim, detect_auc, lexdis_f1, nmf_nmi_type, nmf_nmi_word, passes) |>
  arrange(desc(passes), family, desc(detect_auc)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Finalists on the held-out confirmation bench. Criteria: detect ≥ .845 (surprisal), lexeme-disjoint F1 > .616 (identity), NMF type > word and > .318 (δ)")
```

Only the repair representations meet all four criteria. The geometry and
hidden-state finalists detect errors and type them under supervision, but
their unsupervised components still follow the observed word at least as much
as the error type. Their dimensions also have no names.

# 5. The repair representation

At each token, the model scores about 23 minimal edits:

- other inflections of the word;
- real words within one or two characters;
- its own top predictions as replacements;
- deleting the word;
- inserting one of its top predictions before the word.

Each edit's gain is the change in log-probability (bits) of the edited word
plus the next five subwords, given Study 1's 8-token left window. Edits are
grouped into 29 named classes using closed word lists and simple string
relations. Examples are *insert determiner*, *-s inflection*, *non-word
spelling*, *real-word confusion*, *replace with a preposition*, *replace with
punctuation*, and *delete a content word*.

Two readouts are used:

- **Gains vector.** The best gain per class (positive part), 29 dimensions.
  It is used for essay profiles.
- **Discrete label.** The best edit after a cost of one bit per character
  changed (Shannon's estimate of English entropy, fixed in advance), or NONE
  when no edit pays.

The label is the explanation, and the winning edit is usually the correction
itself.

What it can and cannot see is set by its edit inventory and its window. It
covers single-word substitutions, insertions and deletions within about
thirteen subwords. Word order, multi-word errors and collocational
infelicity land in the broad *replace content word* or *delete content word*
classes, or in NONE.

Cost: about 13 ms of GPU time per token on one A6000, plus candidate
generation on CPU. ELLIPSE's 371k selected tokens took about 1.5 GPU-hours.

# 6. Caveats

- The benchmark's error types are the kinds of error the repair inventory
  targets, so the benchmark favours repair. The real-data checks in the main
  report test whether that advantage holds on learner writing.
- CLEAN_SURP is noisy, since even strong host essays contain natural errors.
- About 45 representations were compared on the development bench, so small
  differences there can be selection noise. The confirmation bench exists for
  this reason.
